materials.name: 304 stainless steel (annealed)
materials.source: handbook typical (AISI 304, annealed). NOT a viable friction rotor: cannot be hardened, k is ~1/3 of carbon steel so heat does not spread, and alpha ~17e-6/K drives large growth/coning

materials.name: 316 stainless steel (annealed)
materials.source: handbook typical (AISI 316, annealed). NOT a viable friction rotor (see 304): low k, high alpha, cannot harden

materials.name: 321 stainless steel (annealed)
materials.source: handbook typical (AISI 321, annealed). NOT a viable friction rotor (see 304)

materials.name: 430 stainless steel (annealed)
materials.source: handbook typical (AISI 430, ferritic annealed). Ferritic: not hardenable by heat treat; better k and lower alpha than austenitic but still weak for a rotor

materials.name: 409 stainless steel (annealed)
materials.source: handbook typical (AISI 409, ferritic). Common in exhaust/heat shields, not friction rotors

materials.name: grey cast iron (Class 30)
materials.source: handbook typical (ASTM A48 Class 30). BRITTLE: the strength figure is TENSILE strength - grey iron has no yield point. Classic rotor material for its damping and thermal capacity
